def port_filters() -> int:
    TARGET_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    count = 0

    for toml_path in sorted(UPSTREAM_DIR.glob("*.toml")):
        with open(toml_path, "rb") as f:
            data = tomli.load(f)

        filters_sec = data.get("filters", {})
        tests_sec = data.get("tests", {})

        for filter_name, filter_info in filters_sec.items():
            if not isinstance(filter_info, dict):
                continue

            if filter_name in CUSTOM_MANAGED_FILTERS:
                # Keep customized high-priority core filter definition
                continue

            test_cases = tests_sec.get(filter_name, [])

            match_cmd = filter_info.get("match_command", "")
            strip_lines = filter_info.get("strip_lines_matching", [])
            keep_lines = filter_info.get("keep_lines_matching", [])
            match_output = filter_info.get("match_output", [])

            # Check regex validity
            for p in [match_cmd] + strip_lines + keep_lines:
                if p:
                    try:
                        re.compile(p)
                    except re.error as e:
                        print(f"Warning: regex error in {toml_path.name}: {p} -> {e}")

            json_data = {
                "name": filter_name,
                "description": filter_info.get("description", ""),
                "match_command": match_cmd,
                "strip_ansi": filter_info.get("strip_ansi", True),
                "strip_lines_matching": strip_lines,
                "keep_lines_matching": keep_lines,
                "match_output": match_output,
                "max_lines": filter_info.get("max_lines"),
                "tail_lines": filter_info.get("tail_lines"),
                "truncate_lines_at": filter_info.get("truncate_lines_at"),
                "on_empty": filter_info.get("on_empty"),
                "source": f"rtk-ai/rtk (src/filters/{toml_path.name})",
                "license": "Apache-2.0",
                "modified": True,
                "tests": [
                    {
                        "name": t.get("name", ""),
                        "input": t.get("input", ""),
                        "expected": t.get("expected", ""),
                    }
                    for t in test_cases
                    if isinstance(t, dict)
                ],
            }

            target_file = TARGET_DIR / f"{filter_name}.json"
            target_file.write_text(json.dumps(json_data, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
            count += 1

    print(f"Successfully ported {count} filters to {TARGET_DIR}")
    return count

def verify_a11y_cmd(
    project_dir: str = typer.Argument(
        ".", help="Project root directory (default: current directory)."
    ),
    src: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--src", help="Subdirectory holding the interface source."
    ),
    report_dir: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--report-dir", help="Directory containing A11Y governance artifacts."
    ),
    warn_only: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--warn-only", help="Report findings without failing exit code."
    ),
    selftest: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--selftest", help="Run built-in fixture test cases."
    ),
    self_test_flag: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--self-test", help="Run built-in fixture test cases (alias)."
    ),
) -> None:
    """Run the A11Y.md static gate to verify artifacts, freshness, contrast math, and source anti-patterns."""
    if selftest or self_test_flag:
        code, msg = verify_a11y_selftest()
        if code == 0:
            console.print(msg, markup=False)
        else:
            err_console.print(msg, markup=False)
        raise typer.Exit(code=code)

    proj_root = Path(project_dir).resolve()
    if not proj_root.is_dir():
        err_console.print(f"error: {proj_root} is not a directory")
        raise typer.Exit(code=2)

    src_path = (proj_root / src).resolve() if src else proj_root
    rep_path = Path(report_dir).resolve() if report_dir else None

    result = run_verify_a11y_checks(
        root=proj_root,
        src=src_path,
        report_dir=rep_path,
        warn_only=warn_only,
    )
    encoding = sys.stdout.encoding or "utf-8"
    out_text = result.output_text.encode(encoding, errors="replace").decode(encoding)
    console.print(out_text, markup=False)
    raise typer.Exit(code=result.exit_code)

def build_docs_plan(graph: CodeGraph, root: Path) -> list[PlanEntry]:
    """Compute the ordered, staleness-annotated doc plan for `graph` with topology enrichment."""
    ordered_nodes = topological_doc_order(graph)

    callers: dict[str, set[str]] = {n.id: set() for n in ordered_nodes}
    callees: dict[str, set[str]] = {n.id: set() for n in ordered_nodes}
    incident_confidences: dict[str, Counter] = {n.id: Counter() for n in ordered_nodes}
    incident_relations: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {
        n.id: [] for n in ordered_nodes
    }
    degrees: dict[str, int] = Counter()

    node_ids = set(callers)
    for edge in graph.edges:
        src = edge.source
        tgt = edge.target
        if src in node_ids:
            degrees[src] += 1
            incident_confidences[src][edge.confidence] += 1
            incident_relations[src].append({"kind": edge.kind, "target": tgt})
        if tgt in node_ids:
            degrees[tgt] += 1
            incident_confidences[tgt][edge.confidence] += 1

        if edge.kind not in _ORDER_EDGE_KINDS:
            continue
        if src not in node_ids or tgt not in node_ids:
            continue
        callees[src].add(tgt)
        callers[tgt].add(src)

    # Detect top god nodes (degree >= 20 and in top 5%)
    degree_sorted = sorted(degrees.values(), reverse=True)
    idx = (
        min(len(degree_sorted) - 1, max(0, len(degree_sorted) // 20))
        if degree_sorted
        else 0
    )
    god_threshold = degree_sorted[idx] if degree_sorted else 20
    god_node_ids = {
        nid for nid, deg in degrees.items() if deg >= max(20, god_threshold)
    }

    plan: list[PlanEntry] = []
    for node in ordered_nodes:
        h = content_hash(node.snippet)
        doc_path = doc_path_for_node(node)
        existing_hash = read_existing_content_hash(root / doc_path)

        cid = node.community_id
        cinfo = graph.communities.get(cid) if cid is not None else None
        clabel = (
            cinfo.label if cinfo else (f"Community {cid}" if cid is not None else None)
        )
        cohesion = cinfo.cohesion if cinfo else None

        plan.append(
            PlanEntry(
                node_id=node.id,
                kind=node.kind,
                name=node.name,
                qualified_name=node.qualified_name,
                file_path=node.file_path,
                language=node.language,
                start_line=node.start_line,
                end_line=node.end_line,
                snippet=node.snippet,
                content_hash=h,
                parent_id=node.parent_id,
                callers=sorted(callers[node.id]),
                callees=sorted(callees[node.id]),
                doc_path=doc_path,
                needs_generation=(existing_hash != h),
                community_id=cid,
                community_label=clabel,
                cohesion=cohesion,
                is_god_node=node.id in god_node_ids,
                degree=degrees.get(node.id, 0),
                signature=node.signature,

def safe_filename(name: str, limit: int = 200) -> str:
    """Sanitize label into a safe filename and verbatim Markdown link destination.

    Substitutes Windows-reserved characters with underscores, collapses whitespace,
    and drops parentheses to keep dunder methods (__init__) and callables readable.

    s = name.replace("/", "-").replace("\\", "-").replace(":", "-").replace(" ", "_")
    s = s.replace("(", "").replace(")", "")

    hub_name: str,
    top_members: list[dict[str, Any]],
    cross_links: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> str:

    lines = ["```mermaid", "flowchart LR"]

    for idx, mem in enumerate(top_members[:6]):

    lines.append("```")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def get_god_nodes(conn: sqlite3.Connection, top_n: int = 10) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Rank highest-degree architectural symbol hubs, filtering noise."""
    query = """
    WITH degree_counts AS (
        SELECT node_id, COUNT(*) as deg FROM (
            SELECT source_id AS node_id FROM edges WHERE kind IN ('calls', 'inherits', 'imports') AND resolved = 1
            UNION ALL
            SELECT target_id AS node_id FROM edges WHERE kind IN ('calls', 'inherits', 'imports') AND resolved = 1
        )
        GROUP BY node_id
    )
    SELECT n.id, n.name, n.kind, n.file_path, n.community_id, d.deg
    FROM nodes n
    JOIN degree_counts d ON n.id = d.node_id
    WHERE n.external = 0 AND n.kind IN ('class', 'function', 'method')
    ORDER BY d.deg DESC
    LIMIT ?
    """
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute(query, (top_n * 2,))
    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for r in cursor.fetchall():
        name = r[1]
        if name in _BUILTIN_NOISE_LABELS:
            continue
        results.append(
            {
                "id": r[0],
                "name": name,
                "kind": r[2],
                "file_path": r[3],
                "community_id": r[4],
                "degree": r[5],
            }
        )
        if len(results) >= top_n:
            break
    return results

def _resolve_inheritance(
    ctx: BuildContext,
    inh: PendingInheritance,
    file_exports: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
    file_imports_map: dict[str, list[str]],
    named_imports_map: dict[str, dict[str, str]],
    global_symbols: dict[str, list[str]],
) -> None:
    target_id: str | None = None
    confidence = CONFIDENCE_EXTRACTED
    conf_score = 1.0

    raw_base = inh.base_name.split(".")[-1]

    # 1. Same-file base class
    same_file_defs = file_exports.get(inh.importing_file_rel, {})
    if inh.base_name in same_file_defs:
        target_id = same_file_defs[inh.base_name]
    elif raw_base in same_file_defs:
        target_id = same_file_defs[raw_base]

    # 2. Named import from another file
    if target_id is None:
        target_file = named_imports_map.get(inh.importing_file_rel, {}).get(raw_base)
        if target_file and target_file in file_exports:
            target_id = file_exports[target_file].get(raw_base)
            confidence = CONFIDENCE_EXTRACTED
            conf_score = 0.95

    # 3. File imports from another module
    if target_id is None:
        for imported_file in file_imports_map.get(inh.importing_file_rel, []):
            if (
                imported_file in file_exports
                and raw_base in file_exports[imported_file]
            ):
                target_id = file_exports[imported_file][raw_base]
                confidence = CONFIDENCE_EXTRACTED
                conf_score = 0.90
                break

    # 4. Global symbol unique match
    if target_id is None and raw_base in global_symbols:
        candidates = global_symbols[raw_base]
        if len(candidates) == 1:
            target_id = candidates[0]
            confidence = CONFIDENCE_INFERRED
            conf_score = 0.75

    if target_id is not None:
        edge = GraphEdge(
            source=inh.source_class_id,
            target=target_id,
            kind=INHERITS,
            resolved=True,
            confidence=confidence,
            confidence_score=conf_score,
            context=CONTEXT_INHERIT,
        )
    else:
        ext = ctx.graph.get_or_create_external(inh.base_name)
        edge = GraphEdge(
            source=inh.source_class_id,
            target=ext.id,
            kind=INHERITS,
            resolved=False,
            confidence=CONFIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS,
            confidence_score=0.2,
            context=CONTEXT_INHERIT,
        )
    ctx.graph.add_edge(edge)

def _resolve_import(
    ctx: BuildContext, imp: PendingImport, file_paths: set[str | None]

    target_rel: str | None = None

    if imp.language == "python":
        target_rel = _resolve_python_import(imp, file_paths)
    elif imp.language in ("javascript", "typescript", "tsx"):
        target_rel = _resolve_js_import(imp, file_paths)
    elif imp.language == "rust":

    elif imp.language in ("java", "kotlin"):

    elif imp.language in ("go", "csharp", "swift"):
        target_rel = _resolve_package_or_namespace_import(imp, file_paths)

    if target_rel is not None:
        edge = GraphEdge(
            source=imp.source_id,
            target=f"file:{target_rel}",
            kind=IMPORTS,
            resolved=True,
            confidence=CONFIDENCE_EXTRACTED,
            confidence_score=1.0,

            resolved=False,

def resolve_mode(filepath: str, task_intent: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Resolves 'auto' mode into a concrete compression profile based on task intent and file size.

    Rules:
    - Active Editing (fix, modify, etc) -> full
    - Mapping (architecture, dependencies, etc) -> map
    - Read-Only (understand, trace, etc) -> signatures
    - Fallback -> file scale (< 4KB = full, >= 4KB = signatures)
    """
    if task_intent:
        intent_lower = task_intent.lower()

        # Active Editing Actions
        editing_keywords = [
            "fix",
            "modify",
            "refactor",
            "change",
            "update",
            "add",
            "implement",
            "edit",
            "write",
        ]
        if any(kw in intent_lower for kw in editing_keywords):
            return "full"

        # Read-Only / Mapping Actions
        map_keywords = [
            "architecture",
            "dependencies",
            "imports",
            "exports",
            "linkages",
            "outline",
        ]
        if any(kw in intent_lower for kw in map_keywords):
            return "map"

        signature_keywords = [
            "find references",
            "understand",
            "trace",
            "call flow",
            "signature",
            "interface",
            "overview",
            "read",
        ]
        if any(kw in intent_lower for kw in signature_keywords):
            return "signatures"

    # Fallback Standard: based on file scale
    try:
        size_bytes = os.path.getsize(filepath)
        if size_bytes < 4096:
            return "full"
        return "signatures"
    except (OSError, FileNotFoundError):
        return "signatures"

def calculate_entropy(text: str) -> float:
    """Calculate the Shannon entropy of a given text.

    H(X) = -sum(P(x_i) * log2(P(x_i)))
    A lower entropy indicates highly repetitive or boilerplate content.
    """
    if not text:
        return 0.0

    counts = Counter(text)
    length = len(text)

    entropy = 0.0
    for count in counts.values():
        probability = count / length
        entropy -= probability * math.log2(probability)

    return entropy

def _get_db_path(cwd: str | None = None) -> Path:
    """Resolve the SQLite graph database path.

    1. Use the command-line override if set.
    2. Traverse upwards from CWD (or given cwd / OVERRIDE_ROOT) to auto-detect .buddhi/graphs/tree-graph.db.
    3. Fallback to (start_dir)/.buddhi/graphs/tree-graph.db if not found.
    """
    if OVERRIDE_DB_PATH is not None:
        return OVERRIDE_DB_PATH

    start_dir = (
        Path(cwd).resolve()
        if cwd
        else (OVERRIDE_ROOT if OVERRIDE_ROOT is not None else Path.cwd().resolve())
    )
    for parent in [start_dir] + list(start_dir.parents):
        for rel in [
            Path(".buddhi") / "graphs" / "tree-graph.db",
            Path(".buddhi") / "tree-graph.db",
            Path(".buddhi") / "graph.db",
        ]:
            candidate = parent / rel
            if candidate.exists():
                return candidate

    # Standard fallback
    return start_dir / ".buddhi" / "graphs" / "tree-graph.db"

def _direct_sql_fallback(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection, query: str, top_n: int = 10
) -> list[SearchResult]:
    """Graceful fallback querying SQLite nodes directly via LIKE."""
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    sql_pattern = f"%{query}%"
    cursor.execute(
        """
        SELECT id, name, kind, file_path, start_line, end_line, signature, snippet, community_id
        FROM nodes
        WHERE external = 0 AND (name LIKE ? OR qualified_name LIKE ? OR snippet LIKE ?)
        LIMIT ?
        """,
        (sql_pattern, sql_pattern, sql_pattern, top_n),
    )
    rows = cursor.fetchall()
    results: list[SearchResult] = []
    for r in rows:
        results.append(
            SearchResult(
                node_id=r[0],
                name=r[1] or "",
                file_path=r[3] or "",
                content=r[7] or "",
                signature=r[6] or "",
                start_line=r[4] or 0,
                end_line=r[5] or 0,
                community_id=r[8] or 0,
                salience_tier="anchor",
                node_type=r[2] or "",
            )
        )
    return results

def _tier3_drop_low_weight(nodes: list[SearchResult]) -> list[SearchResult]:
    if len(nodes) <= 1:
        return nodes

    anchors = [n for n in nodes if n.salience_tier == "anchor"]
    non_anchors = [n for n in nodes if n.salience_tier != "anchor"]
    non_anchors.sort(key=lambda n: n.edge_count, reverse=True)

    keep_count = max(1, len(non_anchors) // 2)
    return anchors + non_anchors[:keep_count]

def expand_query(query: str) -> list[str]:
    """Split a query string into component tokens.

    Handles camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and space-separated terms.
    Filters out tokens shorter than 2 characters.
    """
    tokens: list[str] = []

    for word in query.split():
        parts = word.split("_")
        for part in parts:
            if not part:
                continue
            camel_parts = re.sub(r"([a-z])([A-Z])", r"\1 \2", part)
            camel_parts = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r"\1 \2", camel_parts)
            tokens.extend(camel_parts.split())

    return [t for t in tokens if len(t) >= 2]

def compress_to_budget(nodes: list[SearchResult], budget: int) -> list[SearchResult]:
    output = serialize_context(nodes)
    if count_tokens(output) <= budget:
        return nodes

    # Tier 1: Strip bridges
    nodes = _tier1_strip_bridges(nodes)
    output = serialize_context(nodes)
    if count_tokens(output) <= budget:
        return nodes

    # Tier 2: Degrade modes
    nodes = _tier2_degrade_modes(nodes)
    output = serialize_context(nodes)
    if count_tokens(output) <= budget:
        return nodes

    # Second degradation pass (signatures -> map)
    nodes = _tier2_degrade_modes(nodes)
    output = serialize_context(nodes)
    if count_tokens(output) <= budget:
        return nodes

    # Tier 3: Drop low connectivity nodes
    for _ in range(5):
        prev_count = len(nodes)
        nodes = _tier3_drop_low_weight(nodes)
        output = serialize_context(nodes)
        if count_tokens(output) <= budget or len(nodes) == prev_count:
            break

    return nodes

def u_curve_sort(nodes: list[SearchResult]) -> list[SearchResult]:
    """Reorder nodes using U-Curve positional optimization.

    Layout:
        Top:    anchor nodes (highest salience)
        Middle: bridge nodes (attention dead zone)
        Bottom: community structural boundaries
    """
    if not nodes:
        return nodes

    anchors = [n for n in nodes if n.salience_tier == "anchor"]
    community = [n for n in nodes if n.salience_tier == "community"]
    bridges = [n for n in nodes if n.salience_tier == "bridge"]

    return anchors + bridges + community

def execute_buddhi_search(
    query: str,
    db_path: str,
    top_n: int = 3,
    mode: str = "full",
    include_bridges: bool = True,
    budget: int = 8000,
    root_path: Path | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Search the codebase using Buddhi's topology-driven retrieval pipeline with graceful fallbacks."""
    if not Path(db_path).exists():
        # Graph DB not found -> fallback to native grep
        output = _native_grep_search(query, root_path=root_path)
        if output:
            return output
        return f"Error: Buddhi database not found at '{db_path}' and no native matches found. Please run `buddhi init` first."

    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    try:
        # Phase 1: Lexical Anchor Detection
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        expanded_terms = expand_query(query)
        search_terms = [query] + [
            t for t in expanded_terms if t.lower() != query.lower()
        ]

        anchor_nodes: dict[str, SearchResult] = {}
        anchor_communities: set[int] = set()

        for term in search_terms:
            sql_pattern = f"%{term}%"
            cursor.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, name, kind, file_path, start_line, end_line, signature, snippet, community_id
                FROM nodes
                WHERE external = 0 AND (name LIKE ? OR qualified_name LIKE ?)
                LIMIT ?
                """,
                (sql_pattern, sql_pattern, top_n),
            )
            for r in cursor.fetchall():
                node_id = r[0]
                if node_id not in anchor_nodes:
                    comm_id = r[8] if r[8] is not None else 0
                    if comm_id:
                        anchor_communities.add(comm_id)
                    anchor_nodes[node_id] = SearchResult(
                        node_id=node_id,
                        name=r[1] or "",
                        file_path=r[3] or "",
                        content=r[7] or "",
                        signature=r[6] or "",
                        start_line=r[4] or 0,
                        end_line=r[5] or 0,
                        community_id=comm_id,
                        salience_tier="anchor",
                        node_type=r[2] or "",
                        mode=mode,
                    )
                if len(anchor_nodes) >= top_n:
                    break
            if len(anchor_nodes) >= top_n:
                break

        # Fallback Phase 1b: If no anchors on name/qual, search snippet
        if not anchor_nodes:
            cursor.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, name, kind, file_path, start_line, end_line, signature, snippet, community_id
                FROM nodes
                WHERE external = 0 AND snippet LIKE ?
                LIMIT ?
                """,
                (f"%{query}%", top_n),
            )
            for r in cursor.fetchall():
                node_id = r[0]
                comm_id = r[8] if r[8] is not None else 0

def buddhi_search(
    query: Annotated[
        str,
        "Search query — function names, class names, or natural-language descriptions of code behavior",
    ],
    top_n: Annotated[int, "Number of top lexical anchors to retrieve"] = 3,
    mode: Annotated[
        str,
        "Output mode: 'full' (complete source), 'signatures' (declarations only), or 'map' (one-liner index)",
    ] = "full",
    include_bridges: Annotated[
        bool, "Include 1-hop bridge nodes from neighboring communities"
    ] = True,
    budget: Annotated[int, "Max character count for output. 0 = unbounded"] = 8000,
    cwd: Annotated[
        str | None,
        "Working directory override. Defaults to CWD of the MCP server process.",
    ] = None,
) -> str:
    """Search the codebase using Buddhi's topology-driven retrieval pipeline.

    This replaces standard keyword-only searches with community-aware,
    context-optimized results. It identifies lexical anchors, expands to community
    neighborhoods, filters out boilerplate, and sorts using a U-curve positional layout.
    """
    from buddhi.mcp.tools.search import execute_buddhi_search

    db_path = _get_db_path(cwd)
    root_dir = Path(cwd).resolve() if cwd else OVERRIDE_ROOT
    try:
        return execute_buddhi_search(
            query=query,
            db_path=str(db_path),
            top_n=top_n,
            mode=mode,
            include_bridges=include_bridges,
            budget=budget,
            root_path=root_dir,
        )
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  # noqa: BLE001  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"Error executing search: {e}"

def dump_frontmatter(metadata: dict[str, Any], body: str = "") -> str:
    """Serializes metadata dict into leading --- YAML --- block followed by markdown body."""
    clean_meta = dict(metadata)
    for forbidden in _FORBIDDEN_OKF_FIELDS:
        clean_meta.pop(forbidden, None)

    yaml_str = yaml.safe_dump(
        clean_meta,
        sort_keys=False,
        allow_unicode=True,
        default_flow_style=False,
    ).strip()

    body_clean = body.strip()
    if body_clean:
        return f"---\n{yaml_str}\n---\n\n{body_clean}\n"
    return f"---\n{yaml_str}\n---\n"

def _render_architecture_report(
    root_name: str,
    stats: dict[str, Any],
    god_nodes: list[dict[str, Any]],
    surprises: list[dict[str, Any]],
    questions: list[dict[str, Any]],
    cycles: list[list[str]],
    community_slugs: dict[int, str],
    god_slugs: dict[str, str],
    communities_data: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> str:
    today = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    meta = {
        "type": "Concept",
        "title": "Architecture Report",
        "description": f"Topological codebase audit and architecture analysis for {root_name}.",
        "status": "stable",
        "tags": ["architecture", "code-graph", "audit-report"],
        "generated": {
            "by": "buddhi-docgen",
            "at": today,
            "git_commit": stats.get("built_at_commit", "unknown"),
        },
    }

    conf = stats.get("confidence_breakdown", {})
    total_edges = stats.get("edges", 1) or 1
    ext_pct = round((conf.get("EXTRACTED", 0) / total_edges) * 100)
    inf_pct = round((conf.get("INFERRED", 0) / total_edges) * 100)
    amb_pct = round((conf.get("AMBIGUOUS", 0) / total_edges) * 100)

    body_lines = [
        f"# Architecture Report: {root_name}",
        "",
        "> Topological analysis generated from the Schema v2 Code Graph.",
        "",
        "## Corpus & Graph Health",
        f"- **Graph Size**: {stats.get('nodes', 0)} nodes, {stats.get('edges', 0)} edges across {stats.get('communities', 0)} Leiden communities.",
        f"- **Edge Confidence**: {ext_pct}% EXTRACTED, {inf_pct}% INFERRED, {amb_pct}% AMBIGUOUS.",
        f"- **Git Commit Freshness**: `{stats.get('built_at_commit', 'unknown')[:8]}` (Stale: {stats.get('is_stale', False)}).",
        "",
        "## Community Hubs",
    ]

    comm_map = communities_data or {}
    for cid, slug in sorted(community_slugs.items()):
        clabel = comm_map.get(cid, {}).get("label") or f"Community {cid}"
        body_lines.append(f"- [{clabel}](communities/{slug}.md)")

    body_lines += [
        "",
        "## God Nodes (Core Architectural Abstractions)",
        "The highest incident degree symbols representing load-bearing components:",
        "",
    ]

    for idx, gn in enumerate(god_nodes, 1):
        slug = god_slugs.get(gn["id"], "")
        link = f"[{gn['name']}](god-nodes/{slug}.md)" if slug else gn["name"]
        body_lines.append(
            f"{idx}. **{link}** ({gn.get('degree', 0)} connections) in `{gn.get('file_path', '')}`"
        )

    body_lines += [
        "",
        "## Surprising Connections",
        "Cross-community dependencies and unexpected bridge relationships:",
        "",
    ]
    if surprises:
        for s in surprises:
            rel = s.get("relation", "calls")
            conf_tier = s.get("confidence", "EXTRACTED")
            body_lines.append(
                f"- `{s.get('source', '')}` --{rel}--> `{s.get('target', '')}` `[{conf_tier}]`"
            )
    else:
        body_lines.append(
            "- None detected: all connections are within community boundaries."
        )

    body_lines += [
        "",
        "## Import Cycles",
    ]
    if cycles:
        for c in cycles:
            cycle_str = " -> ".join(c + [c[0]])
            body_lines.append(f"- {len(c)}-file cycle: `{cycle_str}`")
    else:
        body_lines.append("- None detected.")

    body_lines += [
        "",
        "## Suggested Review Questions",
        "_Questions this code graph is uniquely positioned to answer during planning and reviews:_\n",
    ]
    for q in questions:
        body_lines.append(f"- **{q.get('question', '')}**")
        if q.get("target"):
            body_lines.append(f"  _Focus: `{q.get('target', '')}`_")

    return dump_frontmatter(meta, "\n".join(body_lines))

def generate_search_index(docs_dir: Path, output_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Scan docs_dir markdown files and emit search-index.json into output_dir."""
    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    if docs_dir.is_dir():
        for md_file in sorted(docs_dir.rglob("*.md")):
            try:
                text = md_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
                data, _ = split_frontmatter(text)
                rel_path = md_file.relative_to(docs_dir)
                html_url = rel_path.with_suffix(".html").as_posix()
                entries.append(
                    {
                        "title": data.get("title") or md_file.stem,
                        "kind": data.get("type") or data.get("kind", "concept"),
                        "summary": data.get("description") or data.get("summary", ""),
                        "url": html_url,
                        "tags": data.get("tags") or [],
                        "status": data.get("status", "stable"),
                        "community": data.get("community_id"),
                    }
                )
            except OSError:
                continue

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    index_file = output_dir / "search-index.json"
    index_file.write_text(json.dumps(entries, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return index_file

def extract_a11y_decisions(a11y_decisions_path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Extracts (title, rationale, date) from A11Y-DECISIONS.md entries."""
    if not a11y_decisions_path.is_file():
        return []

    text = a11y_decisions_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    entries: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []

    pattern = re.compile(
        r"^[ \t]*[-*]\s*\*\*(.+?)\*\*\s*(?:[—–\->:]+)?\s*(.+?)(?:\s*\(([^)]+)\))?$",
        re.MULTILINE,
    )
    for m in pattern.finditer(text):
        title = m.group(1).strip()
        body = m.group(2).strip()
        date_str = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        if (
            not title
            or "example — replace with your project's first real decision" in body
        ):
            continue
        entries.append((title, body, date_str))

    return entries

def sanitize_slug(raw_slug: str) -> str:
    """Sanitize slug for safe cross-platform file naming."""
    # Replace path separators and special characters with dash
    clean = raw_slug.replace("/", "-").replace("\\", "-")
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_-]+", "-", clean.lower()).strip("-_")
    if not slug or slug in WINDOWS_RESERVED or slug == "..":
        slug = f"mem-{slug}" if slug else "mem-node"
    return slug[:60]

    """Return node/edge counts, confidence breakdown, and git staleness."""
    meta = dict(conn.execute("SELECT key, value FROM meta").fetchall())

def get_surprising_connections(
    conn: sqlite3.Connection, top_n: int = 10
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Rank edges by composite surprise score."""
    caps = get_db_capabilities(conn)
    conf_col = (
        "e.confidence" if caps["has_edge_confidence"] else "'EXTRACTED' AS confidence"
    )

    query = f"""
    SELECT
        e.source_id, e.target_id, e.kind, {conf_col},
        s.file_path AS s_file, s.community_id AS s_comm,
        t.file_path AS t_file, t.community_id AS t_comm,
        s.name AS s_name, t.name AS t_name
    FROM edges e
    JOIN nodes s ON e.source_id = s.id
    JOIN nodes t ON e.target_id = t.id
    WHERE e.kind IN ('calls', 'inherits') AND e.resolved = 1 AND s.external = 0 AND t.external = 0
    LIMIT 1000
    """
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    cursor.execute(query)

    scored: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for r in cursor.fetchall():
        (
            source_id,
            target_id,
            kind,
            confidence,
            s_file,
            s_comm,
            t_file,
            t_comm,
            s_name,
            t_name,
        ) = r
        score = 0.0

        # Cross-community bridge
        if s_comm is not None and t_comm is not None and s_comm != t_comm:
            score += 0.40

        # Cross top-level directory
        s_dir = (s_file or "").split("/")[0] if s_file else ""
        t_dir = (t_file or "").split("/")[0] if t_file else ""
        if s_dir and t_dir and s_dir != t_dir:
            score += 0.25

        # Confidence bonus
        if confidence == "AMBIGUOUS":
            score += 0.25
        elif confidence == "INFERRED":
            score += 0.15

        if score > 0.3:
            scored.append(
                {
                    "source": source_id,
                    "target": target_id,
                    "kind": kind,
                    "confidence": confidence,
                    "source_name": s_name,
                    "target_name": t_name,
                    "source_file": s_file,
                    "target_file": t_file,
                    "surprise_score": round(score, 2),
                }
            )

    scored.sort(key=lambda x: -x["surprise_score"])
    return scored[:top_n]

def write_sqlite(
    graph: CodeGraph,
    path: Path,
    *,
    root_path: str,
    extract_cache_entries: list[tuple[str, str, str, str, str]] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Atomically write CodeGraph to SQLite database (Schema v2)."""
    tmp_path = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.tmp-{os.getpid()}")
    tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    conn = sqlite3.connect(tmp_path)
    try:
        conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)
        conn.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO nodes (id, kind, name, qualified_name, file_path, language, "
            "start_line, end_line, parent_id, signature, external, snippet, community_id) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (
                (
                    n.id,
                    n.kind,
                    n.name,
                    n.qualified_name,
                    n.file_path,
                    n.language,
                    n.start_line,
                    n.end_line,
                    n.parent_id,
                    n.signature,
                    int(n.external),
                    n.snippet,
                    n.community_id,
                )
                for n in graph.nodes.values()
            ),
        )

        conn.executemany(
            "INSERT INTO edges (source_id, target_id, kind, resolved, confidence, confidence_score, context) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (
                (
                    e.source,
                    e.target,
                    e.kind,
                    int(e.resolved),
                    e.confidence,
                    float(e.confidence_score),
                    e.context,
                )
                for e in graph.edges
            ),
        )

        if graph.communities:
            conn.executemany(
                "INSERT INTO communities (id, label, node_count, cohesion, hub_node_id, top_files) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    (
                        c.id,
                        c.label,
                        c.node_count,
                        float(c.cohesion),
                        c.hub_node_id,
                        json.dumps(c.top_files, ensure_ascii=False),
                    )
                    for c in graph.communities.values()
                ),
            )

        if extract_cache_entries:
            conn.executemany(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO extract_cache (file_path, sha256, language, payload_json, updated_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                extract_cache_entries,
            )

        meta_entries = [
            ("schema_version", SCHEMA_VERSION),
            ("generated_at", datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()),
            ("root_path", root_path),
            ("node_count", str(len(graph.nodes))),
            ("edge_count", str(len(graph.edges))),
            ("community_count", str(len(graph.communities))),
            ("built_at_commit", graph.built_at_commit or ""),
        ]
        conn.executemany("INSERT INTO meta (key, value) VALUES (?, ?)", meta_entries)
        conn.commit()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    # Retry replace for Windows file locks
    for attempt in range(4):
        try:
            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
            break
        except PermissionError:
            if attempt == 3:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.025 * (attempt + 1))

    q_file = get_queue_file(layer, run_id, project_root)

    try:
        with open(q_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:

                    data = json.loads(line)
                    intents.append(

                            old_string=data.get("old_string"),

                            reason=data.get("reason", ""),
                            evidence=data.get("evidence", ""),
                            absorbed_into=data.get("absorbed_into"),
                        )
                    )
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        pass
    return intents

def evaluate_lifecycle(
    skills: dict[str, SidecarData],
    current_request_count: int,
    layer: str = "project",
    capacity_limit: int | None = None,
    maturity_limit: int | None = None,
) -> LifecycleDecision:
    """Evaluate skill pool and determine which skills to keep and which to archive."""
    maturity = maturity_limit or MATURITY_THRESHOLD.get(layer, 100)
    capacity = capacity_limit or CAPACITY.get(layer, 50)

    keep: list[str] = []
    to_archive: list[str] = []

    # 1. Graduation review: mature skills with use == 0 and view == 0 get archived
    graduates: list[tuple[str, float]] = []

    for name, sidecar in skills.items():
        tenure = max(0, current_request_count - sidecar.anchor)

        # Still in probation
        if tenure < maturity:
            keep.append(name)
            continue

        # Mature: check usage
        if sidecar.use == 0 and sidecar.view == 0:
            to_archive.append(name)
        else:
            denom = max(1, tenure)
            rate = sidecar.use / denom
            graduates.append((name, rate))

    # 2. Capacity eviction among active graduates
    if len(graduates) > capacity:
        # Sort by rate ascending, tie-break by deterministic sha256 of name
        graduates.sort(
            key=lambda item: (
                item[1],
                hashlib.sha256(item[0].encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
            )
        )
        excess = len(graduates) - capacity
        evicted = [g[0] for g in graduates[:excess]]
        retained = [g[0] for g in graduates[excess:]]
        to_archive.extend(evicted)
        keep.extend(retained)
    else:
        keep.extend([g[0] for g in graduates])

    return LifecycleDecision(keep=sorted(keep), archive=sorted(to_archive))

def stage_skill(
    action: Annotated[
        str, "Action: 'create', 'update', 'patch', 'remove_file', or 'delete'"
    ],
    name: Annotated[str, "Skill identifier (lowercase, hyphenated)"],
    layer: Annotated[str, "Target layer: 'project' (default) or 'global'"] = "project",
    body: Annotated[str | None, "Full Markdown body including YAML frontmatter"] = None,
    old_string: Annotated[
        str | None, "Exact target text to replace (for 'patch')"
    ] = None,
    new_string: Annotated[str | None, "Replacement text (for 'patch')"] = None,
    files: Annotated[
        dict[str, str] | None, "Relative subfile mapping {filepath: content}"
    ] = None,
    reason: Annotated[str, "Why this mutation is needed"] = "",
    evidence: Annotated[
        str, "Concrete log/code evidence demonstrating the problem/rule"
    ] = "",
    absorbed_into: Annotated[
        str | None, "Target surviving umbrella skill name (for 'delete')"
    ] = None,
    cwd: Annotated[str | None, "Workspace root override"] = None,
) -> str:
    """Stage a self-learned skill mutation into the AutoHarness intent queue for admission validation and promotion."""
    from buddhi.scripts.autoharness.intent_queue import append_intent
    from buddhi.scripts.autoharness.models import SkillIntent

    if action not in ("create", "update", "patch", "remove_file", "delete"):
        return f"Error: Invalid action '{action}'. Must be one of create, update, patch, remove_file, delete."

    if not name:
        return "Error: Skill name is required."

    if action in ("create", "update") and not body:
        return f"Error: Action '{action}' requires a Markdown body."

    if action == "patch" and (not old_string or new_string is None):
        return "Error: Action 'patch' requires 'old_string' and 'new_string'."

    if action != "delete" and not evidence.strip():
        return f"Error: Action '{action}' requires non-empty 'evidence'."

    if not reason.strip():
        return f"Error: Action '{action}' requires non-empty 'reason'."

    if action == "delete" and not absorbed_into:
        return "Error: Action 'delete' requires 'absorbed_into' naming the surviving skill."

    intent = SkillIntent(
        action=action,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        name=name,
        layer=layer if layer in ("project", "global") else "project",  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        body=body,
        old_string=old_string,
        new_string=new_string,
        files=files or {},
        reason=reason,
        evidence=evidence,
        absorbed_into=absorbed_into,
    )

    project_root = (
        Path(cwd).resolve() if cwd else (OVERRIDE_ROOT or Path.cwd().resolve())
    )
    try:
        append_intent(intent, run_id="interactive", project_root=project_root)
        return f"[AutoHarness] Staged intent '{action} {name}'. Will be validated and landed on turn completion."
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"Error staging skill intent: {exc}"

def slice_transcript_window(
    transcript_path: Path,
    offset: int = 0,
) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Seek to byte offset in transcript.jsonl, clip lines, and redact secrets/PII."""
    if not transcript_path.is_file():
        return "", offset

    collected_records: list[str] = []
    total_bytes = 0

    with open(transcript_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        f.seek(offset)
        new_offset = f.tell()

        for line in f:
            new_offset = f.tell()
            line_str = line.strip()
            if not line_str:
                continue

            # Clip individual line length
            clipped = line_str[:MAX_RECORD_BYTES]
            collected_records.append(clipped)
            total_bytes += len(clipped)

            if total_bytes >= MAX_WINDOW_BYTES:
                break

    raw_text = "\n".join(collected_records)
    redacted_text = redact_text(raw_text)
    return redacted_text, new_offset

def archive_skill(skills_dir: Path, name: str) -> Path:
    """Move skill directory to .archive/<timestamp>-<name>/."""
    src = skills_dir / name
    if not src.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Skill '{name}' does not exist.")

    archive_root = skills_dir / ARCHIVE_DIRNAME
    archive_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    timestamp = int(time.time())
    dest = archive_root / f"{timestamp}-{name}"
    counter = 1
    while dest.exists():
        dest = archive_root / f"{timestamp}-{name}-{counter}"
        counter += 1

    shutil.move(str(src), str(dest))
    return dest

def check_all_files(max_tokens: int = 8000) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    """Scan all tracked files in git index.

    Returns (exit_code, output_lines).
    """
    max_bytes = max_tokens * 4
    try:
        raw_files = run_git(["ls-files", "-z"]).split("\0")
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError) as exc:
        return 2, [f"error: failed running git ls-files: {exc}"]

    files = [f for f in raw_files if f.strip() and is_source_file(f)]
    unauthored_files = get_unauthored(files)
    candidates = [f for f in files if f not in unauthored_files]

    violations: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
    opted_out = 0

    for path in candidates:
        size = blob_bytes(f":{path}")
        if size is not None and size > max_bytes:
            if is_ignored(f":{path}"):
                opted_out += 1
            else:
                violations.append((path, size))

    violations.sort(key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True)

    lines: list[str] = []
    for path, size in violations:
        tok_str = format_tokens(size).rjust(15)
        lines.append(f"{tok_str}  {path}")

    lines.append(f"Source files over {max_tokens:,} tokens: {len(violations)}.")
    if opted_out > 0:
        lines.append(f"Over the budget but opted out with {PRAGMA}: {opted_out}.")

    exit_code = 1 if violations else 0
    return exit_code, lines

def claims_in(line: str, line_idx: int, previous: str = "") -> list[ClaimHit]:
    lower = line.lower()
    carried = previous.lower()[-60:]
    hits: list[ClaimHit] = []

    for match in NUMBER_RE.finditer(line):
        value, suffix = match.groups()
        start = match.start()
        before = f"{carried} " if start < 40 else ""
        before += lower[max(0, start - 40) : start]
        after = lower[start + len(match.group(0)) : start + len(match.group(0)) + 24]
        context = f"{before} {after}"

        unit_attached = suffix == "%" or bool(suffix)
        unit_nearby = any(
            re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(u)}\b", context) for u in MEASUREMENT_UNITS
        )
        verb_nearby = any(v in before for v in MEASUREMENT_VERBS)

        if not unit_attached and not unit_nearby and not verb_nearby:
            continue
        hits.append(
            ClaimHit(
                line_idx=line_idx,
                value=value,
                text=match.group(0).strip(),
                column=start + 1,
                is_hex=False,
            )
        )

    for match in HEX_RE.finditer(line):
        hits.append(
            ClaimHit(
                line_idx=line_idx,
                value=match.group(1).lower(),
                text=match.group(1),
                column=match.start() + 1,

def rtk_filters_test_cmd(
    filter_name: Annotated[str, typer.Argument(help="Name of the filter to test.")],
) -> None:
    """Run embedded test cases for a specific RTK filter."""
    from buddhi.scripts.rtk.engine import apply_filter
    from buddhi.scripts.rtk.filters import load_builtin_filters

    filters = load_builtin_filters()
    target = next((f for f in filters if f.name == filter_name), None)

    if target is None:
        err_console.print(f"[red]error:[/red] filter '{filter_name}' not found.")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    if not target.tests:
        console.print(f"[dim]Filter '{filter_name}' has no embedded test cases.[/dim]")
        return

    console.print(
        f"[bold cyan]Running {len(target.tests)} test(s) for filter '{filter_name}':[/bold cyan]"
    )
    failed = 0
    for idx, t in enumerate(target.tests, 1):
        actual = apply_filter(t.input, target)
        norm_actual = actual.strip().replace("\r\n", "\n")
        norm_exp = t.expected.strip().replace("\r\n", "\n")
        if norm_actual == norm_exp:
            console.print(f"  [green]PASS[/green] ({idx}) {t.name}")
        else:
            console.print(f"  [red]FAIL[/red] ({idx}) {t.name}")
            console.print(f"    Expected: {norm_exp!r}")
            console.print(f"    Got:      {norm_actual!r}")
            failed += 1

    if failed > 0:
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)
    console.print(f"[bold green]All {len(target.tests)} test(s) passed.[/bold green]")

def apply_generic_filter(
    raw_output: str,
    max_lines: int = DEFAULT_GENERIC_MAX_LINES,
    head_lines: int = DEFAULT_HEAD_LINES,
    tail_lines: int = DEFAULT_TAIL_LINES,
) -> str:
    """Filter arbitrary command output using generic heuristics without losing error context."""
    if not raw_output:
        return ""

    cleaned = strip_ansi(raw_output)
    lines = cleaned.splitlines()

    lines = collapse_blank_lines(lines)
    lines = collapse_duplicate_lines(lines)

    if len(lines) <= max_lines:
        return "\n".join(lines).strip()

    # If exceeding max_lines, separate error lines so they are never lost
    head = lines[:head_lines]
    tail = lines[-tail_lines:] if tail_lines > 0 else []

    middle_lines = (
        lines[head_lines:-tail_lines] if tail_lines > 0 else lines[head_lines:]
    )
    omitted_count = len(middle_lines)

    # Collect any error lines that occurred in the omitted middle
    salvaged_errors: list[str] = []
    for line in middle_lines:
        if is_error_line(line):
            salvaged_errors.append(line)

    result_parts: list[str] = []
    result_parts.extend(head)

    omitted_notice = f"\n[... {omitted_count} lines omitted ...]\n"
    if salvaged_errors:
        omitted_notice += f"[... {len(salvaged_errors)} error/failure line(s) salvaged from omitted section: ...]\n"
        omitted_notice += "\n".join(salvaged_errors) + "\n"

    result_parts.append(omitted_notice.strip())
    result_parts.extend(tail)

    return "\n".join(result_parts).strip()

def is_rewrite_candidate(command: str) -> bool:
    """Check whether a command is a candidate for output filtering."""
    stripped = command.strip()

    # Check prefix wrappers like 'uv run <cmd>' or 'poetry run <cmd>'
    m = re.match(r"^(?:uv\s+run|poetry\s+run)\s+(.*)$", stripped)
    inner = m.group(1).strip() if m else stripped

    try:
        parts = shlex.split(inner, posix=False)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        parts = inner.split()

    if not parts:
        return False

    prog = os.path.basename(parts[0]).lower()
    if prog.endswith((".exe", ".cmd", ".bat")):
        prog = prog.rsplit(".", 1)[0]

    # Check against known default rewrite commands
    if prog in DEFAULT_REWRITE_COMMANDS:
        allowed_subs = DEFAULT_REWRITE_COMMANDS[prog]
        if allowed_subs is None:
            return True
        if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1] in allowed_subs:
            return True

    # Check against any active builtin filter
    filters = load_builtin_filters()
    return find_matching_filter(stripped, filters) is not None

def aggregate_savings(ledger_path: Path = DEFAULT_LEDGER_PATH) -> SavingsSummary:
    """Aggregate token savings statistics from the ledger."""
    total_runs = 0
    total_raw = 0
    total_filtered = 0
    total_saved = 0
    by_command: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

    if ledger_path.is_file():
        try:
            with open(ledger_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                for line in f:
                    line = line.strip()
                    if not line:
                        continue
                    try:
                        entry = json.loads(line)
                    except json.JSONDecodeError:
                        continue

                    raw_tok = entry.get("raw_tokens", 0)
                    filt_tok = entry.get("filtered_tokens", 0)
                    saved_tok = entry.get("saved_tokens", raw_tok - filt_tok)
                    cmd = entry.get("command", "other")
                    filter_name = entry.get("filter_name", "unknown")

                    total_runs += 1
                    total_raw += raw_tok
                    total_filtered += filt_tok
                    total_saved += max(0, saved_tok)

                    cat = f"{cmd} ({filter_name})"
                    if cat not in by_command:
                        by_command[cat] = {
                            "runs": 0,
                            "raw": 0,
                            "filtered": 0,
                            "saved": 0,
                        }

                    by_command[cat]["runs"] += 1
                    by_command[cat]["raw"] += raw_tok
                    by_command[cat]["filtered"] += filt_tok
                    by_command[cat]["saved"] += max(0, saved_tok)

        except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.warning("Failed to read ledger from %s: %s", ledger_path, err)

    percentage = (total_saved / total_raw * 100.0) if total_raw > 0 else 0.0

    return SavingsSummary(
        total_runs=total_runs,
        total_raw_tokens=total_raw,
        total_filtered_tokens=total_filtered,
        total_saved_tokens=total_saved,
        savings_percentage=round(percentage, 1),
        by_command=by_command,
    )

    json_mode: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--json", help="Output token savings summary as JSON."
    ),

    table.add_row("Overall Reduction", f"{summary.savings_percentage}%")

                f"{stats['filtered']:,}",
                f"{saved_t:,}",
                f"{pct}%",
            )

        console.print(breakdown_table)

def trust_filter_file(path: Path, trust_store: Path = DEFAULT_TRUST_STORE) -> str:
    """Record the current SHA-256 hash of a filter file into the trust store."""

        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Filter file not found: {path}")

    current_hash = compute_filter_hash(path)
    trusted = get_trusted_hashes(trust_store)

def check_report_status(report: Path, findings: list[GateFinding]) -> None:
    body = body_of(report)
    unchecked = len(re.findall(r"^\s*-\s*\[\s\]", body, re.MULTILINE))
    failed = len(re.findall(r"^\s*-\s*\[!\]", body, re.MULTILINE))

    field = re.search(
        r"(?:Compliance Status|Status de Conformidade):?\*{0,2}[ \t]*(.*)",
        body,

    )
    value = field.group(1).strip() if field else ""

        findings.append(
            GateFinding(
                "ERROR",
                "report-status",

                "(the PASS | CONDITIONAL | FAIL menu). Declare one status.",

        findings.append(
            GateFinding(

                "report-status",

def _chunk(chunk_type: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    length = struct.pack(">I", len(data))
    crc = struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(chunk_type + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return length + chunk_type + data + crc

    """Encode raw RGBA buffer into standard 8-bit PNG bytes."""

    # Prepend filter byte 0 (None) to each row
    stride = width * 4
    raw_scanlines = bytearray()
    for y in range(height):
        raw_scanlines.append(0)  # Filter byte None
        start = y * stride
        raw_scanlines.extend(data[start : start + stride])

    compressed = zlib.compress(bytes(raw_scanlines), level=6)
    idat = _chunk(b"IDAT", compressed)
    iend = _chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return PNG_SIGNATURE + ihdr + idat + iend

def compute_scene_metrics(img: RawImage) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Compute coarse-grid scene composition metrics for an image."""
    step_x = max(1, img.width // 160)
    step_y = max(1, img.height // 90)
    cols = img.width // step_x
    rows = img.height // step_y
    if cols < 2 or rows < 2:
        return None

    gray_samples: list[float] = []
    buckets: dict[tuple[int, int, int], int] = {}
    samples = 0
    transparent = 0

    for gy in range(rows):
        for gx in range(cols):
            o = (gy * step_y * img.width + gx * step_x) * 4
            alpha = img.data[o + 3] / 255.0
            if alpha == 0:
                transparent += 1
            r = img.data[o] * alpha
            g = img.data[o + 1] * alpha
            b = img.data[o + 2] * alpha
            lum = luminance(r, g, b)
            gray_samples.append(lum)

            bucket = (int(r) >> 4, int(g) >> 4, int(b) >> 4)
            buckets[bucket] = buckets.get(bucket, 0) + 1
            samples += 1

    sorted_gray = sorted(gray_samples)
    mean = sum(sorted_gray) / len(sorted_gray)
    p5 = sorted_gray[int(len(sorted_gray) * 0.05)]
    p95 = sorted_gray[int(len(sorted_gray) * 0.95)]

    entropy = 0.0
    dominant = 0
    for count in buckets.values():
        p = count / samples
        entropy -= p * math.log2(p)
        dominant = max(dominant, count)

    edges = 0
    checked = 0
    for gy in range(rows - 1):
        for gx in range(cols - 1):
            i = gy * cols + gx
            dx = abs(gray_samples[i] - gray_samples[i + 1])
            dy = abs(gray_samples[i] - gray_samples[i + cols])
            if max(dx, dy) > 12:
                edges += 1
            checked += 1

    return {
        "colorBuckets": len(buckets),
        "colorEntropyBits": round(entropy, 4),
        "edgeDensity": round(edges / checked if checked else 0, 4),
        "dominantColorShare": round(dominant / samples if samples else 0, 4),
        "transparentShare": round(transparent / samples if samples else 0, 4),
        "luminanceMean": round(mean, 4),
        "luminanceP5": round(p5, 4),
        "luminanceP95": round(p95, 4),
        "luminanceContrast": round(p95 - p5, 4),
    }

def selftest() -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Verify PNG encode/decode roundtrip and metrics calculation."""
    # Synthetic 4x4 image
    width, height = 4, 4
    raw_data = bytearray(width * height * 4)
    for i in range(width * height):
        raw_data[i * 4] = (i * 16) & 0xFF
        raw_data[i * 4 + 1] = (i * 32) & 0xFF
        raw_data[i * 4 + 2] = (i * 48) & 0xFF
        raw_data[i * 4 + 3] = 255

    encoded = encode_png_rgba(width, height, raw_data)
    decoded = decode_png(encoded)
    assert decoded.width == width
    assert decoded.height == height
    assert decoded.data == raw_data

    # Compare identical images
    metrics = compute_scene_metrics(decoded)
    assert metrics is not None
    assert "colorBuckets" in metrics
    return 0, "selftest: visual-parity-diff OK"

def sobel_magnitude(
    gray: list[float], width: int, height: int, x: int, y: int
) -> float:
    xm = max(0, x - 1)
    xp = min(width - 1, x + 1)
    ym = max(0, y - 1)
    yp = min(height - 1, y + 1)

    a = gray[ym * width + xm]
    b = gray[ym * width + x]
    c = gray[ym * width + xp]
    d = gray[y * width + xm]
    f = gray[y * width + xp]
    g = gray[yp * width + xm]
    h = gray[yp * width + x]
    i = gray[yp * width + xp]

    gx = (c + 2 * f + i) - (a + 2 * d + g)
    gy = (g + 2 * h + i) - (a + 2 * b + c)
    return min(255.0, math.sqrt(gx * gx + gy * gy))

def visual_parity_diff_cmd(
    candidate_dir: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--candidate-dir", help="Directory of candidate PNG captures."
    ),
    reference_dir: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--reference-dir", help="Directory of reference PNG captures."
    ),
    out_dir: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--out-dir", help="Output directory for diff artifacts and JSON."
    ),
    crops_json: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--crops-json", help="Path to crop coordinates JSON."
    ),
    report_order: str | None = typer.Option(
        None, "--report-order", help="Comma-separated image stems for ordering."
    ),
    selftest: bool = typer.Option(False, "--selftest", help="Run self-test."),
) -> None:
    """Run visual parity diffing or solo scene-metrics telemetry."""
    if selftest:
        code, msg = visual_parity_diff_selftest()
        if code == 0:
            console.print(msg)
        else:
            err_console.print(msg)
        raise typer.Exit(code=code)

    cand = candidate_dir or os.environ.get("CANDIDATE_DIR")
    ref = reference_dir or os.environ.get("REFERENCE_DIR")
    out = out_dir or os.environ.get("OUT_DIR") or "visual-diff"
    crops = crops_json or os.environ.get("CROPS_JSON")
    order_str = report_order or os.environ.get("REPORT_ORDER") or ""

    if not cand:
        err_console.print(
            "error: --candidate-dir or CANDIDATE_DIR environment variable is required."
        )
        raise typer.Exit(code=2)

    cand_path = Path(cand).resolve()
    if not cand_path.is_dir():
        err_console.print(f"error: candidate directory does not exist: {cand_path}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=2)

    ref_path = Path(ref).resolve() if ref else None
    if ref_path and not ref_path.is_dir():
        err_console.print(f"error: reference directory does not exist: {ref_path}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=2)

    order_list = (
        [s.strip() for s in order_str.split(",") if s.strip()] if order_str else None
    )
    crops_path = Path(crops).resolve() if crops else None

    code, report = run_visual_parity_diff(
        candidate_dir=cand_path,
        reference_dir=ref_path,
        out_dir=Path(out).resolve(),
        report_order=order_list,
        crops_json=crops_path,
    )
    if code != 0:
        err_console.print(f"error: {report.get('error', 'visual diff failed')}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=code)

    console.print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
    raise typer.Exit(code=0)

def resolve_template(template_name: str, repo_root: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Resolve a template name to a file path using the priority stack.

    Order:
      1. .agents/templates/overrides/
      2. .agents/templates/
      3. .specify/templates/overrides/
      4. .specify/templates/
    """
    if not _is_safe_component(template_name):
        return None

    for base in [
        repo_root / ".agents" / "templates",
        repo_root / ".specify" / "templates",
    ]:
        override = base / "overrides" / f"{template_name}.md"
        if override.is_file():
            return override
        core = base / f"{template_name}.md"
        if core.is_file():
            return core

    return None

def diff_agents_md(old_content: str, new_content: str) -> str:
    """Generate a clean unified diff between old and new AGENTS.md content."""
    old_lines = old_content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    new_lines = new_content.splitlines(keepends=True)

        fromfile="a/AGENTS.md",
        tofile="b/AGENTS.md",

    return "".join(diff_gen)

def parse_agents_sections(content: str) -> list[AgentsSection]:
    """Parse an AGENTS.md markdown string into structured sections."""
    lines = content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    sections: list[AgentsSection] = []

    current_heading = ""
    current_level = 0
    current_lines: list[str] = []

    header_re = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$")

    for line in lines:
        match = header_re.match(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        # Only split on level 1 or level 2 headers for major sections
        if match and len(match.group(1)) <= 2:
            if current_heading or current_lines:
                norm_h = current_heading.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
                is_managed = norm_h in _MANAGED_HEADINGS or norm_h.startswith(
                    "agents.md"
                )
                sections.append(
                    AgentsSection(
                        heading=current_heading,
                        level=current_level,
                        content="".join(current_lines),
                        is_managed=is_managed,
                    )
                )
            current_heading = line.strip()
            current_level = len(match.group(1))
            current_lines = []
        else:
            current_lines.append(line)

    if current_heading or current_lines:
        norm_h = current_heading.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
        is_managed = norm_h in _MANAGED_HEADINGS or norm_h.startswith("agents.md")
        sections.append(
            AgentsSection(
                heading=current_heading,
                level=current_level,
                content="".join(current_lines),
                is_managed=is_managed,
            )
        )

    return sections

def merge_agents_md(existing_content: str, facts: RepoFacts) -> MergeResult:
    """Safely merge newly detected repo facts into an existing AGENTS.md.

    Preserves all unmanaged custom user sections byte-for-byte in their original order.
    """
    sections = parse_agents_sections(existing_content)
    if not sections:
        # File is empty, generate from scratch
        from buddhi.skills.agents_md.generator import generate_agents_md

        new_content = generate_agents_md(facts)
        diff_str = diff_agents_md(existing_content, new_content)
        return MergeResult(
            content=new_content,
            diff=diff_str,
            has_changes=bool(diff_str),
            updated_sections=[
                "# AGENTS.md",
                "## Commands",
                "## Agent Conventions & Skills",
            ],
        )

    updated_sections: list[str] = []
    preserved_sections: list[str] = []
    out_parts: list[str] = []

    has_seen_commands = False
    has_seen_conventions = False

    for sec in sections:
        norm_h = sec.heading.lstrip("#").strip().lower()

        if norm_h.startswith("agents.md") or sec.level == 1:
            # Top-level title and description blockquote
            out_parts.append(sec.heading + "\n")
            # If the user has a custom blockquote, preserve or update smoothly
            if facts.description and ">" in sec.content:
                # Update blockquote line while keeping surrounding layout
                desc = facts.description.strip()
                if not desc.endswith("."):
                    desc += "."
                new_body_lines: list[str] = []
                for line in sec.content.splitlines(keepends=True):
                    if line.strip().startswith(">"):
                        new_body_lines.append(f"> {facts.name} - {desc}\n")
                    else:
                        new_body_lines.append(line)
                out_parts.append("".join(new_body_lines))
            else:
                out_parts.append(sec.content)
            updated_sections.append(sec.heading)

        elif norm_h == "commands":
            has_seen_commands = True
            out_parts.append(sec.heading + "\n")
            out_parts.append(_build_commands_body(facts))
            updated_sections.append(sec.heading)

        elif norm_h in (
            "agent conventions & skills",
            "agent conventions",
            "skills & architecture",
        ):
            has_seen_conventions = True
            out_parts.append(sec.heading + "\n")
            out_parts.append(_build_conventions_body(facts))
            updated_sections.append(sec.heading)

        else:
            # Unmanaged custom section: PRESERVE VERBATIM
            out_parts.append(sec.heading + "\n")
            out_parts.append(sec.content)
            preserved_sections.append(sec.heading)

    # If Commands or Conventions were not present in existing file, append them
    if not has_seen_commands:
        out_parts.append("\n## Commands\n")
        out_parts.append(_build_commands_body(facts))
        updated_sections.append("## Commands")

    if not has_seen_conventions:
        out_parts.append("\n## Agent Conventions & Skills\n")
        out_parts.append(_build_conventions_body(facts))
        updated_sections.append("## Agent Conventions & Skills")

    merged_content = "".join(out_parts)
    # Normalize ending with single newline
    if not merged_content.endswith("\n"):
        merged_content += "\n"

    diff_str = diff_agents_md(existing_content, merged_content)

    return MergeResult(
        content=merged_content,
        diff=diff_str,
        has_changes=bool(diff_str),
        updated_sections=updated_sections,
        preserved_sections=preserved_sections,
    )

def diff_design_md(old_content: str, new_content: str) -> str:
    """Generate a clean unified diff between old and new DESIGN.md content."""
    old_lines = old_content.splitlines(keepends=True)
    new_lines = new_content.splitlines(keepends=True)

        old_lines,
        new_lines,
        fromfile="a/DESIGN.md",
        tofile="b/DESIGN.md",
    )
    return "".join(diff_gen)

def parse_design_sections(markdown_body: str) -> list[DesignSection]:
    """Parse Markdown content into structured sections based on H1-H3 headers."""
    lines = markdown_body.splitlines(keepends=True)
    sections: list[DesignSection] = []

    current_heading = ""
    current_level = 0
    current_lines: list[str] = []

    header_re = re.compile(r"^(#{1,3})\s+(.*)$")

    for line in lines:
        match = header_re.match(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if match:
            if current_heading or current_lines:
                norm_h = current_heading.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
                is_managed = norm_h in _MANAGED_HEADINGS or norm_h.startswith(
                    "design system"
                )
                sections.append(
                    DesignSection(
                        heading=current_heading,
                        level=current_level,
                        content="".join(current_lines),
                        is_managed=is_managed,
                    )
                )
            current_heading = line.strip()
            current_level = len(match.group(1))
            current_lines = []
        else:
            current_lines.append(line)

    if current_heading or current_lines:
        norm_h = current_heading.lstrip("#").strip().lower()
        is_managed = norm_h in _MANAGED_HEADINGS or norm_h.startswith("design system")
        sections.append(
            DesignSection(
                heading=current_heading,
                level=current_level,
                content="".join(current_lines),
                is_managed=is_managed,
            )
        )

    return sections

def extract_command(payload):
    """Pull the shell command string out of a tool-call payload, if any.

    The field holding the command text varies by tool/hook shape, so check
    a few known locations in order. This hook only ever backstops
    shell/terminal-command-shaped tool calls (run_command, git-specialist
    shells out, etc.) — if none of those fields are present (or the payload
    isn't a dict), this is not a command invocation at all (e.g. a Write/Edit
    of file content), and there is nothing to safely pattern-match against:
    return None rather than stringifying the whole payload, which would
    otherwise deny file writes whose *content* merely mentions a destructive
    command (including this harness's own rule docs).
    """
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        for key in ("command", "cmd"):
            value = payload.get(key)
            if isinstance(value, str):
                return value

        for outer_key, inner_key in (
            ("input", "command"),
            ("tool_input", "command"),
            ("parameters", "command"),
            ("input", "cmd"),
            ("tool_input", "cmd"),
            ("parameters", "cmd"),
        ):
            outer = payload.get(outer_key)
            if isinstance(outer, dict):
                inner = outer.get(inner_key)
                if isinstance(inner, str):
                    return inner

    return None

def _ensure_skill_frontmatter(content: str, default_name: str) -> str:
    """Ensure content has valid YAML frontmatter containing 'name' and 'description'."""
    match = re.match(r"^---\r?\n(.*?)\r?\n---\r?\n(.*)$", content, flags=re.DOTALL)
    if not match:
        desc = f"Custom skill migrated from {default_name}."
        lines = content.strip().splitlines()
        for line in lines:
            if line.startswith("# "):
                title = line.lstrip("# ").strip()
                desc = f"Skill for {title}. Migrated from {default_name}."
                break
        return f"---\nname: {default_name}\ndescription: {desc}\n---\n\n{content}"

    fm_raw = match.group(1)
    body = match.group(2)

    has_name = re.search(r"^name:\s*", fm_raw, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    has_desc = re.search(r"^description:\s*", fm_raw, flags=re.MULTILINE)

    fm_lines = [line for line in fm_raw.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if not has_name:
        fm_lines.insert(0, f"name: {default_name}")
    if not has_desc:
        fm_lines.append(f"description: Custom skill migrated from {default_name}.")

    new_fm = "\n".join(fm_lines)
    return f"---\n{new_fm}\n---\n{body}"

    """Ensure `.buddhi/` and `.buddhi/graphs/` exist under root; return the graphs dir.

    buddhi_dir = root / BUDDHI_DIR_NAME

def migrate_legacy_plan_skill(
    agents_dir: Path, project_root: Path | None = None
) -> PlanMigrationReport:
    """Migrate legacy .agents/skills/plan to .agents/skills/spec-plan and update references.

    1. Directory Migration:
       - If .agents/skills/plan exists and .agents/skills/spec-plan does not exist:
         Moves .agents/skills/plan to .agents/skills/spec-plan, updating its frontmatter
         ('name: plan' -> 'name: spec-plan', '# /plan' -> '# /spec-plan').
       - If .agents/skills/plan exists and .agents/skills/spec-plan already exists:
         Removes .agents/skills/plan to prevent collision with Antigravity's built-in /plan.

    2. Reference Updates:
       - Safely updates '/plan' references to '/spec-plan' across:
         * project_root / 'AGENTS.md' (if present)
         * agents_dir / 'rules' / 'harness-core.md'
         * agents_dir / 'skills' / 'specify' / 'SKILL.md'
         * agents_dir / 'skills' / 'implement' / 'SKILL.md'
         * agents_dir / 'skills' / 'README.md'
       - Uses regex boundary matching (?<![a-zA-Z0-9_/-])/plan(?![a-zA-Z0-9_/-])
         ensuring commands like /quick-plan, plan.md, or buddhi docs plan are never touched.
    """
    report = PlanMigrationReport()
    plan_dir = agents_dir / "skills" / "plan"
    spec_plan_dir = agents_dir / "skills" / "spec-plan"

    if plan_dir.is_dir():
        if not spec_plan_dir.exists():
            try:
                shutil.move(str(plan_dir), str(spec_plan_dir))
                report.migrated_skill = True

def sync_template_tree(src_dir: Path, dest_dir: Path) -> TemplateSyncReport:
    """Copy every file under `src_dir` into `dest_dir`, preserving relative paths.

    Never overwrites a file that already exists at the destination — a file
    once written there may have been hand-edited by the user, and buddhi has
    no way to distinguish "untouched since last init" from "customized", so
    the safe default is to leave any existing file alone and only fill in
    what's missing.
    """
    report = TemplateSyncReport()
    if not src_dir.is_dir():
        raise BuddhiFsError(f"template source missing: {src_dir}")

    for src_path in sorted(src_dir.rglob("*")):
        if src_path.is_dir():
            continue
        if "__pycache__" in src_path.parts:
            continue
        if src_path.suffix in (".pyc", ".pyo"):
            continue
        if src_path.name == "__init__.py":
            # The template tree is itself a Python package (so it can be
            # packaged/imported), but __init__.py exists only for that
            # purpose — it is not harness content and must never be
            # scaffolded into a target project's `.agents/`.
            continue
        rel = src_path.relative_to(src_dir)
        dest_path = dest_dir / rel
        try:
            dest_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            if dest_path.exists():
                report.kept_existing.append(dest_path)
                continue
            shutil.copyfile(src_path, dest_path)
            report.created.append(dest_path)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise BuddhiFsError(f"could not write {dest_path}: {exc}") from exc

    return report

def test_init_scaffolds_all_23_new_skills_and_preserves_customizations(tmp_path: Path):
    # Create sample codebase
    (tmp_path / "main.py").write_text("print('hello world')\n", encoding="utf-8")

    result = runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(tmp_path)])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, f"init failed: {result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"

    skills_dir = tmp_path / ".agents" / "skills"
    assert skills_dir.is_dir()

    # 1. Assert all 23 new skills exist with valid frontmatter
    for skill_name in NEW_SKILLS_23:
        skill_dir = skills_dir / skill_name
        assert skill_dir.is_dir(), f"Skill directory missing: {skill_name}"
        skill_file = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"
        assert skill_file.is_file(), f"SKILL.md missing for: {skill_name}"
        content = skill_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        m = re.match(r"^---\r?\n(.*?)\r?\n---\r?\n", content, re.DOTALL)
        assert m is not None, f"YAML frontmatter missing in {skill_name}/SKILL.md"
        fm = m.group(1)
        assert (
            f"name: {skill_name}" in fm
            or f"name: '{skill_name}'" in fm
            or f'name: "{skill_name}"' in fm
        ), f"name mismatch in {skill_name}"
        assert "description:" in fm, f"description missing in {skill_name}"

    # 2. Assert selective custom skills are NOT copied by init
    for custom_skill in CUSTOM_SKILLS_NOT_IN_INIT:
        assert not (skills_dir / custom_skill).exists(), (
            f"Custom skill {custom_skill} should not be in init"
        )

    # 3. Assert supporting reference files were copied
    assert (
        skills_dir / "explore-unknowns" / "references" / "stage-1-known-knowns.md"
    ).is_file()
    assert (
        skills_dir / "compare-screenshots" / "references" / "reference-landmarks.md"
    ).is_file()
    assert (skills_dir / "audit-agents" / "assets" / "example-agents.md").is_file()

    # 4. Modify a skill file to test idempotency
    target_skill_file = skills_dir / "explore-unknowns" / "SKILL.md"
    custom_content = "# CUSTOMIZED BY USER\n" + target_skill_file.read_text(
        encoding="utf-8"
    )
    target_skill_file.write_text(custom_content, encoding="utf-8")

    # Re-run init
    result2 = runner.invoke(app, ["init", str(tmp_path)])
    assert result2.exit_code == 0

    # Ensure custom content was preserved (not overwritten)
    assert target_skill_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").startswith(
        "# CUSTOMIZED BY USER"
    )
